title: San Francisco Oracle, vol. 1 no. 10, cover
lede: The front page of the Haight-Ashbury underground newspaper, October 1967: a mandala of rings and checkerboards in magenta, violet, and turquoise on newsprint.
summary: October 1967. Concentric mandala, swollen ORACLE masthead, and warped checkerboards in three inks on newsprint.

source.label: Internet Archive: San Francisco Oracle Vol. 1 No. 10 (Daniel D. Teoli Jr. Archival Collection)

creator.name: The Oracle of the City of San Francisco (Allen Cohen, editor); cover artist not identified

evidence.note: Downloaded page 1 of the Teoli scan (2704 × 4073 px) to a scratch folder and inspected it. The cover is signed at lower center with a name I could not read, dated ’67. The Letterform Archive scans of other issues on Internet Archive are stream-only. The image is not stored.

styles.note: A clear example in newsprint: every part of the page is patterned, the masthead swells to fill an arch, and magenta, violet, and turquoise sit side by side.

context: The Oracle was an underground newspaper published in 12 issues from September 1966 to February 1968 in the Haight-Ashbury, edited by Allen Cohen with Michael Bowen as art director. Wikipedia calls it “arguably the outstanding example of psychedelia” in the underground press. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Oracle).

From issue 6 the paper was printed at Howard Quinn Printers, where its artists perfected the split-fountain rainbow effect by damming the ink fountain to feed several colors at once. The print run peaked at about 125,000. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Oracle).
The Internet Archive item states a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license from the scanning collector. That license covers the scan, not the 1967 artwork.
observed: ORACLE fills an arch across the top in fat turquoise letters with violet shadows and outlines. THE CITY OF SAN FRANCISCO curves above it in smaller letters.
A large mandala of concentric rings, lobes, and interlocking circles fills the middle. Its center is a small target of tight rings.
Warped checkerboards in magenta, violet, turquoise, and paper color fill every corner and recede like a tunnel.
An embracing couple drawn in rough outline stands at the bottom center, under a figure-eight sign.
The inks are magenta, violet, and turquoise on yellowed newsprint. Prices, the date, and the issue number are lettered by hand into the pattern.
interpretation: This page meets all four diagnostics of the rubric: complementary colors side by side, a swollen masthead, a symmetrical central medallion, and rings and patterns that fill the background.
Low-cost three-ink newsprint produced the same effect as the poster work, which suggests the look depends on arrangement more than on premium printing.
borrow: Arch a fat masthead over a central mandala and let pattern fill the rest.
Use a warped checkerboard that recedes toward the center to give depth without shading.
Letter small facts, such as price and date, into the pattern instead of into a separate box.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The cover artwork is in copyright or of unknown status; the artist is not identified. The CC BY-NC-ND license on the Internet Archive item applies to the scan only.
